title: Gm-C filter pole
description: One transconductor-capacitor integrator pole, $f_c = g_m/(2*\pi*C_{int})$, sized from the cutoff spec. $g_m$ is pinned from $f_c$ into the integrating cap with an over-design factor; $g_m/I_D$ is the efficiency knob. The transconductor's $V^*$ is reported as a small-signal linear-range proxy, the integrated input noise (thermal floor plus a $1/f$ tail) is checked against a budget, and the resulting dynamic range is estimated. Assumes a single dominant pole and a simple differential transconductor; the true large-signal linearity depends on the Gm cell topology and is sim-owned. Feeds a downstream filter sheet that cascades these poles.

params.name: od_factor
params.note: over-design factor on gm for parasitic pole loading and PVT

params.name: vds
params.note: transconductor drain bias, signed to the table axis

params.name: fco_est
params.note: flicker corner estimate; read fco from the table when it carries noise PSDs

params.name: f_hi
params.note: noise integration band, high edge (typically the passband edge)

params.name: V_sig_pk
params.note: peak input signal amplitude for the dynamic-range estimate

params.name: ft_margin
params.note: how many times faster than f_c the transconductor must be

rows.name: V_lin
rows.note: V* as a small-signal linear-range proxy; true linearity is topology-dependent, estimate

rows.name: vn_int
rows.note: integrated input noise over the band: thermal floor plus a 1/f tail with corner fco_est

rows.name: DR_dB
rows.note: dynamic range: max signal over integrated noise; estimate, sim confirms with distortion

rows.name: ft_dev
rows.note: transconductor transit frequency from its own gate cap

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
transconductor stays in saturation with headroom
estimate-grade: uses V* as the linearity proxy; distortion sign-off is sim-owned
the transconductor's fT must clear the pole it sets with margin; estimate-grade
